source: Hand-curated by Hackmons Hub from the Pokemon Speedrunning community's route documents (github.com/pokemon-speedrunning/speedrun-routes), the PSR Discord 'Gen 1 Resources' pins and public YouTube searches. Every video was confirmed through YouTube's oEmbed endpoint (title and channel) and yt-dlp (upload date) on the date in 'verified'. A Trainer ID with no entry here has no published manipulation on record and the tools say so; an entry here credits the original author and never implies they endorse these tools.

documented.label: Original source
documented.text: A published manipulation of this exact Trainer ID exists; it is the original source, and the route shown here is only a rendering of the same target.

community.label: Community list
community.text: This Trainer ID is served from the Pokemon Speedrunning community's published buffered-input list; no video or write-up for this exact ID is on record here.

derived.label: Derived
derived.text: No published manipulation of this Trainer ID is on record here; the route shown was derived by Hackmons Hub's own tooling and has not been confirmed by anyone else.

entry_fields: games: the game keys the source applies to | tid: 4 upper-case hex digits, or null for a source that documents the method without one ID | title / author / url / date (YYYY-MM-DD, null when the page carries none) / kind (video, wiki, guide, forum, list, route) / what (one sentence) | console, note, route {title, url}, sequence (the input sequence the source states, in the community list grammar): optional | verified: the day the url was confirmed | tools: the community timer programs the cues stand in for (id, name, author, url, links, what), credited by id wherever a page offers a cue or timer

tools.name: EonTimer
tools.author: Toast++ (ToastPlusOne), 2010; ported and maintained by DasAmpharos
tools.what: the community's countdown timer for Pokemon RNG manipulation: Gen 3 standard and variable-target timers, the Gen 4 delay timer with its second and delay calibration, the Gen 5 boot-second, C-Gear and Entralink timers, and custom multi-phase timers; the Gen 3 dead-battery timer and the Gen 4 two-phase timer on these pages are ports of its models (MIT per its README).
tools.license: MIT per its README (no license file on the main branch on the day verified)

tools.name: FlowTimer
tools.author: stringflow
tools.what: the speedrunning community's beep-and-flash countdown timer, described by its author as a more accurate EonTimer clone with more functionality for speedrunning: offsets, a beep interval and count, custom timer files; the offsets the Gen 1-3 route documents and videos quote are FlowTimer offsets, and the count-in cues here play the same role.

beyond.why: Every method in this app is the same shape: a stock console, a clock you can read, and a moment to press a button. That shape runs out after Gen 5. From Gen 6 the Trainer ID still comes from a seed, but nothing on screen tells you what the seed is - the community reads it off the running console with homebrew instead. There is no press for this app to hand you, so it stops rather than pretend.
beyond.also: And two of the Switch games are not waiting on anyone: their Trainer ID comes from a cryptographically secure generator, which is not manipulable by construction. That is a fact about the games, not a gap in the tooling.

generations.games: X, Y, Omega Ruby, Alpha Sapphire
generations.what: Trainer ID manipulation is solved and tooled. 3DSRNGTool covers Gen 6 ID RNG directly. What it cannot do is tell you the seed: that is read off the running console by a plugin under NTR custom firmware.

generations.games: Sun, Moon, Ultra Sun, Ultra Moon
generations.what: The same picture as Gen 6: 3DSRNGTool covers Gen 7 ID RNG, and the seed comes from a homebrew reader rather than from anything visible in the game.

The Trainer ID and Secret ID are drawn from a cryptographically secure generator. There is no seed to predict and no timing that changes the answer. Other RNG in these games (raid dens) is a separate and very much solved subject - the Trainer ID is not.
The exception among the Switch games: Trainer ID and Secret ID manipulation does work here, and the community has written it up. It still needs custom firmware to see the state.

Same as Sword and Shield for the Trainer ID: a cryptographically secure generator, so there is nothing to manipulate. Plenty of OTHER RNG manipulation works in this game - outbreaks and mass outbreaks - which is why it is easy to read that it 'has RNG manip' and assume the Trainer ID is included.

This project did not find a clear answer for the Trainer ID in Scarlet and Violet, so it is not going to state one. Raid seed manipulation in these games is well documented; whether the Trainer ID can be targeted is a separate question and the place to ask it is the community, not this page.
